documentation.title: Contact patch test across NON-MATCHING interface meshes (2D, mortar segmentation)
documentation.description:
The contact patch test in its full form: uniform pressure transmitted exactly across an interface whose two sides are meshed DIFFERENTLY. The lower body has five elements along the interface, the upper three, so secondary elements straddle primary element boundaries.
The Poisson ratio is zero, which is what turns this into a patch test: the exact solution of the loaded column is then uniform uniaxial stress and the exact contact pressure is exactly the applied 1e6 Pa at every point. The expected answer is known analytically and independent of the mesh, so any deviation is pure discretization error.
This is the gate on mortar segmentation. With segmentation="gpts" the integration points are the secondary element's own, so a point near a primary boundary carries a weight computed for the whole secondary element: the RESULTANT stays exact -- it depends only on the weights summing to the area -- but the pressure distribution comes out several percent too high on this mesh pairing. With the default segmentation="mortar" the secondary elements are cut along the projected primary outlines and the pressure is transmitted exactly.
The two assertions are complementary: maxPressure = 1e6 exact only WITH mortar segmentation totalContactForce = 2e6 exact either way, by equilibrium; cannot be fooled by discretization
